# drawbridge — game and game-adjacent domains
#
# App installs are stopped by `blocked_packages`; this list closes the browser
# route to the same games, and the Minecraft Bedrock multiplayer servers.
#
# NOTE ON MINECRAFT: the game itself is deliberately NOT blocked — neither the
# package nor minecraft.net. Only Realms and the large public Bedrock servers
# are listed. A DNS blocklist cannot stop a server joined by raw IP address, and
# it cannot enumerate the thousands of small servers that exist, so this is a
# speed bump rather than a wall. Treat single-player and LAN as allowed.

# Roblox
roblox.com
rbxcdn.com
roblox.qq.com

# Fortnite / Epic
fortnite.com
epicgames.com
unrealengine.com
easyantcheat.net

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# European Parent Safety Catalogue — added with policy 21.
#
# Publisher domains where the publisher only makes games, game domains where
# the game has its own site. Every entry below was resolved before being added;
# candidates that had lapsed to squatters or to an unrelated business were
# dropped rather than listed. Notably absent for that reason: frostpunkmobile.com
# (now a gambling site, and covered by the gambling list anyway), wwemayhem.com
# (a fan forum), nuverse.com (a financial firm, not the games publisher).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ============================================================================
# Web games, added 2026-08-17 on the owner's list.
#
# The app side of games is covered by the store rule, which blocks Play's
# GAME_* categories outright. This is the browser side, and it is a different
# problem: a mini-game site needs no install, so nothing the app blocker does
# reaches it. It will stay leaky in the way any domain list is leaky — the
# long tail here is endless and mostly regional. That is a known property
# rather than a defect to be fixed by adding a thousand names.
#
# Every domain below was fetched on 2026-08-17 and its page title had to be
# the site it claims to be. Five are behind bot protection and could not be
# read — newgrounds.com, speeleiland.nl, spelle.be, logicieleducatif.fr and
# construct.net — and are included anyway on the hiwaifu.com precedent, each
# name being distinctive enough to belong to nothing else.
# ============================================================================

# --- the big portals ---
poki.com
crazygames.com
y8.com
miniclip.com
armorgames.com
kongregate.com
newgrounds.com
kizi.com
silvergames.com
lagged.com
addictinggames.com
coolmathgames.com
friv.com
gamesgames.com
jeux.fr
nitrome.com
arkadium.com
plays.org
htmlgames.com
gamesnacks.com

# --- chess: deliberately NOT blocked ---
# Both were on the original list and both came straight back off it on the
# owner's call of 2026-08-17. The argument for blocking them was the engagement
# machinery — rating ladders, streaks, blitz timers — and the argument against
# is simply that chess is not what this list is for.
#
# lichess.org came off with chess.com rather than being asked about separately:
# it is the free, ad-free, open-source one, so blocking it while allowing the
# commercial one would have been backwards.
#
# lichess.org
# chess.com

# --- educational games ---
# Judgement call, and a real one: several of these are used by schools,
# so a child told to do homework on topmarks.co.uk will find it blocked.
# They are here because they are games with a curriculum attached, and
# the owner's rule is that games go. Delete lines to disagree.
abcya.com
funbrain.com
kids.nationalgeographic.com
natgeokids.com
coolmath4kids.com
mathplayground.com
topmarks.co.uk
ictgames.com
starfall.com
education.com
arcademics.com
turtlediary.com
primarygames.com
lululataupe.com
jeuxpedago.com
logicieleducatif.fr
wordwall.net

# --- making games, not playing them ---
# The awkward corner of this list. Scratch, Blockly, code.org, Construct
# and Unity Play teach programming — and they also host thousands of
# finished games playable in the browser, which is what puts them here.
# The cost is real and is worth knowing before somebody hits it.
scratch.mit.edu
code.org
blockly.games
construct.net
play.unity.com

# --- indie hosts ---
itch.io
gamejolt.com

# --- HELD BACK, deliberately not blocked -------------------------------------
# These four were on the owner's list, were held back, and the hold was
# **confirmed by the owner on 2026-08-17**: blocking them is not the point.
#
# DNS cannot see a path, so blocking a domain blocks all of it — and for these
# the games are a small corner of something much larger. Verified 2026-08-17:
#
#   vrt.be                 the Flemish public broadcaster — VRT NWS and VRT MAX sit here
#   ouders.ketnet.be       literally *Ketnet for parents*: a resource for the adult, not games
#   bbc.co.uk              the whole BBC — News, iPlayer, World Service
#   archive.org            the Internet Archive: a library, the Wayback Machine, books and audio
#
# Left commented rather than deleted so that nobody adds them back without
# meeting the reason first. Including them costs the phone the BBC, the VRT, the
# Internet Archive, and a page written for parents. herald's own
# `blocked_url_patterns` is the tool that could reach only the games paths —
# but it works in herald alone, which fails the rule policy 55 set when Ecosia
# was dropped: an engine is only as forced as its weakest browser.
#
# vrt.be
# ouders.ketnet.be
# bbc.co.uk
# archive.org
